## What is cumulative frequency? {#l2-cumulative-definition .compact .cumulative-definition}

::: {.takeaway}
The **cumulative frequency** is the total number of outcomes **less than or equal to a given outcome**. It is a **running total**.
:::

::: {.split .cf-example-layout}
::: {.column-block}

A survey of **50 households**:

| Number of pets, $x$ | Frequency, $f$ |
|:---:|:---:|
| 0 | 15 |
| 1 | 20 |
| 2 | 10 |
| 3 | 4 |
| 4 | 1 |

:::
::: {.column-block}

At $x=2$, include every household with **0, 1 or 2 pets**.

$$cf=15+20+10=45.$$

**45 households have at most 2 pets.**

We can also take the previous cumulative frequency and add the current frequency:

$$cf=35+10=45.$$

:::
:::

<p class="small-note">Each new entry: <span data-math="\text{new }cf=\text{previous }cf+\text{current }f">new cf = previous cf + current f</span>.</p>

::: notes
Use the teacher's definition before introducing the extra table column. Outcomes here means observed outcomes, including repetitions: count households, not the number of distinct pet-count values. The three highlighted rows show x≤2: 15+20+10=45 households have at most two pets. Compare this with the ordinary frequency of 10, which counts exactly two pets. Reuse the previous cumulative total at x=1, namely 35, then add the current frequency 10. The next row will use 45+4=49. Start the first row from a cumulative total of 0. Keep integer values in ascending order.
:::
